findings.title: Cancel promotes unknown outer-worker evidence to cancelled
findings.trigger: outerWorkerView returns false because no worker PID has been claimed yet or a live worker's current start identity cannot be read, while writer.json still contains the valid pre-Host not_started phase.
findings.impact: cancel reports a terminal cancellation, unlinks the launch-bound lock, and releases the fence even though asynchronous work can continue; recovery becomes false success rather than an explicit outcome_unknown freeze.
findings.evidence: The branch is gated by !view.alive rather than a proven-stopped outer-worker state. writerBoundaryState can legitimately return stopped for not_started even though the detached outer worker exists between spawn and lock claim. Direct fixtures observed result_failure_type cancelled, lock_exists false, and fence_count 0.
findings.suggestion: Keep cancel.request creation first, then branch on an explicit outer-worker state. On unknown, return cancel_requested without synthesizing a result, deleting the lock, or releasing the fence; only the stopped state may execute lines 1195 through 1206.

positive_observations: The canonical cancel signal is written before mutable worker-spec consumption and refuses symlink targets.
When the inner writer observation is unknown, the candidate already publishes outcome_unknown and retains the physical fence.
limitations: This lens did not promote the retained cross-platform raw-PID limitation beyond P2; it addresses only the newly confirmed safe-terminal release path.
